record.original_question: Remove the current smoothness restrictions in KAM-based arguments and prove non-transitivity and non-mixing properties for the three-dimensional Euler equation in full generality.

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Relax the restrictions on the smoothness index k of the C k spaces (related to appli- cation of the KAM) and prove non-transitivity and non-mixing properties of the 3D Euler in full generality. It turns out that the Euler equations on higher-dimensional Riemannian manifolds possess a kind of universal embedding property, somewhat similar to the theorems of Whitney and Nash on embeddings of manifolds as submanifolds in higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces. Namely, it was shown in [135] that a certain large class of finite-dimensional quadratic dy- namical systems in Rd can be realized as subsystems of the hydrodynamical Euler equation on the manifold SO(d) × Td+1 with a certain metric depending on the original system. Subsequently, Torres de Lizaur in [138] proved that such a realization is possible for any dynamical system of a finite-dimensional manifold or for its approximation. This way essentially any finite-dimensional dynamical system or its approximation to an arbitrary degree can be embedded as an invariant (tiny) subsystem in a higher-dimensional Euler equation for a certain metric. The construction in [138], which has already found other applications, goes as follows: for a given finite-dimensional dynamical system one first embeds it via Whitney to a system on a submanifold inside a higher-dimensional torus, extends it hyperbolically to a dynamical system in the torus, and then writes it via the smooth vector field (represented by a Fourier series) in that torus. artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a closed Riemannian 3-manifold and consider the incompressible Euler equation on $M$:
$$\partial_t u + \nabla_u u = -\nabla p, \qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
acting on the space $\mathcal{X}^k(M)$ of divergence-free vector fields of class $C^k$. Let $\Phi_t^E:\mathcal{X}^k(M)\to\mathcal{X}^k(M)$ denote the (locally defined) Euler flow.

The flow is said to be transitive on a set $U\subset\mathcal{X}^k(M)$ if for every nonempty open $V_1,V_2\subset U$ there exists $t\ge 0$ with $\Phi_t^E(V_1)\cap V_2\ne\emptyset$, and it is said to be mixing if for any two nonempty open sets $V_1,V_2$ one has $\Phi_t^E(V_1)\cap V_2\ne\emptyset$ for all sufficiently large $t$.

Existing KAM-based arguments establish non-transitivity and non-mixing of the 3D Euler flow only under restrictions on the regularity index $k$ (typically $k>4$ and non-integer, sufficient to apply KAM theory to the Lagrangian flow of steady states).

Problem. Remove these smoothness restrictions: prove non-transitivity and non-mixing of the incompressible Euler equation on closed Riemannian 3-manifolds for the $C^k$ topology in full generality (in particular, for all relevant integer values of $k$ and for low-regularity classes not currently covered by KAM methods).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is recognized as open in its full generality. Original non-mixing results (Khesin–Misiołek–Shnirelman, ARMA 2020) require $C^k$ with $k>4$ non-integer, due to KAM. Subsequent work (Cardona–Miranda–Peralta-Salas and "The Euler non-mixing made easy", 2024) extends non-mixing using contact-geometric methods, weakening some smoothness assumptions, but the goal of fully removing the KAM-induced regularity restrictions has not been completely achieved.

status_evidence.title: Global, Local and Dense Non-mixing of the 3D Euler Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Non-mixing in C^k topology for k>4 non-integer, using KAM theory.
status_evidence.claim: Original non-mixing result has KAM-imposed smoothness restrictions.

status_evidence.title: The Euler non-mixing made easy
status_evidence.snippet: Solves a problem posed by Khesin, Misiolek, and Shnirelman about non-mixing in lower smoothness using contact geometry.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress lowering the smoothness requirement via contact geometry, but not full generality.

status_evidence.title: Contact type solutions and non-mixing of the 3D Euler equations
status_evidence.snippet: Develops contact-geometric route to non-mixing complementing KAM-based arguments.
status_evidence.claim: Active area with progress beyond KAM-only methods.
